newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says Thompson union accepts deal.
newsitem.headline: Inco says Thompson union accepts deal.

text.p: Inco Ltd said that the union at its Thompson, Manitoba, nickel facility had approved on Sunday a three-year labor agreement that had been tentatively reached two days earlier.
Inco spokesman Mark Tessier told Reuters that 70 percent of the membership voted to accept it.
"Operations will resume with the start of the day shift on Monday," he said.
Tessier said Inco kept all its customers supplied during the 15-day lockout, working with them when necessary to provide alternative sources.

He would not say how much production was lost but said the Thompson facility produces about 100 million pounds of nickel a year, about 20 percent of Inco's total output. Given its 11- month production schedule, a 15-day stoppage would cut output by about 4.5 million pounds.
Inco had imposed a lockout on September 15. The main issue in the contract dispute involving the 1,400 workers was shift scheduling.

Tessier said the United Steelworkers of America local agreed to allow shifts to be up to 12 hours instead of the present eight in the mines and the utility unit. This will save the company money by cutting down on transportation time to and from the mines, he added.
Union members will get a 35 Canadian cent raise in the hourly pay for the first year, with no increase for the second and third years, except to adjust for inflation.
However, the cost of living adjustment will now be rolled into the base pay every six months instead of at the end of the agreement as in the past contract.
Union spokesman Nelson Pruder confirmed by telephone that the deal had been accepted with the raise as described by Tessier.
